evidence.dominant_driver: Renewed risk that US 10-year Treasury yields retest 5% as high real yields, issuance pressure and oil-related inflation risk persist into the FOMC

market_expectations.distribution_notes: A September hike is already near fully priced, so residual market sensitivity is increasingly about guidance and whether long yields sustain or break above 5%.

absorption.reason: US10Y already traded above 5% on Monday and then faded below it; the article adds a fresh framework for a retest rather than a new data shock.

observed_reaction.DXY: firm near a two-week high around 99.55
observed_reaction.US_equities: Monday close was already weaker, with S&P 500 -0.48% and Nasdaq -0.56%

observations.WTI: about 102-103 USD/bbl in latest contemporaneous reports
observations.BRENT: about 107 USD/bbl in latest contemporaneous reports

evidence.decision_notes: Residual-move forecast only. This is analysis/commentary, not a fresh release. The 5% yield shock has already occurred once, so short-horizon directional confidence is capped; renewed yield confirmation would matter more than the headline itself. No M2 learning segment was used to change confidence because no clearly applicable ACTIONABLE model-2 evidence segment was established from the leakage-safe profile.

immediate.rationale: The 5% yield shock is partly priced, limiting a clean immediate residual call.

next_session.rationale: FOMC guidance and whether US10Y sustains above 5% dominate the next session.

15m.rationale: Commentary arrives after the first 5% test; without a fresh yield breakout the residual impulse is weak.

1h.rationale: A renewed move toward 5% in long yields would pressure long-duration technology valuations.

4h.rationale: Pre-FOMC positioning around the 5% yield threshold creates asymmetric two-way volatility risk.

next_session.rationale: A hike is heavily priced; guidance and the long-end reaction matter more than the expected decision.

predictions.mechanism: Higher real discount rates compress long-duration technology valuations.
predictions.invalidation: US10Y decisively retreats from 5% while DXY softens and risk appetite improves.
predictions.counter_case: Because the first 5% break already failed and a hike is near fully priced, a yield retreat can trigger a technology relief rally.

technical_state.trend_1h: rate pressure remains elevated but no fresh breakout confirmed

immediate.rationale: High yields are bearish but the major repricing preceded this commentary.

next_session.rationale: Near-full hike pricing raises relief-rally risk if long yields fail to break higher.

15m.rationale: No new data shock and substantial prior absorption reduce immediate edge.

1h.rationale: A 5% US10Y retest would renew broad multiple compression and risk-off pressure.

4h.rationale: The 5% threshold and FOMC proximity favor unstable two-way price action over a clean trend.

next_session.rationale: The expected hike is largely priced and the yield response will determine direction.

predictions.mechanism: Higher real yields pressure broad equity multiples while high oil sustains inflation risk.
predictions.invalidation: Sustained fall in US10Y and oil with a softer dollar.
predictions.counter_case: A failed 5% retest can ease financial-condition fears and produce a broad relief rally.

immediate.rationale: High real yields and firm USD are bearish, but geopolitical and oil risk support haven demand.

next_session.rationale: Rates and haven demand remain in direct conflict into the FOMC.

15m.rationale: The rates story is partly priced and gold faces offsetting haven demand.

1h.rationale: A renewed US10Y/DXY push higher would increase the opportunity-cost headwind for gold.

4h.rationale: A 5% yield retest versus Middle East risk creates competing strong drivers.

next_session.rationale: FOMC guidance, real yields and geopolitical headlines can pull gold in opposite directions.

predictions.mechanism: Higher real yields and USD pressure gold while geopolitical supply risk supports safe-haven demand.
predictions.invalidation: A sharp yield/DXY reversal or fresh material Middle East escalation would favor upside instead.
predictions.counter_case: If the 5% yield level rejects again or Hormuz risk escalates, safe-haven buying can overpower the rates headwind.
